title: AdTech real-time personalization pilot: deployment proposal & pricing
body:
Context and objective:

Customer: DSPCo (demand-side platform focused on programmatic display + connected TV).
Primary ask: run a 6-week pilot to validate real-time (sub-200ms) personalization at scale using Redwood inference runtime, measure cost/latency tradeoffs, and produce an integration path for production deployment (Dedicated or Private).

High-level goals (what success looks like):
- End-to-end inference path from bid request -> context enrichment -> personalization model call -> scoring returned to bidder within target SLO (P90 <= 200ms).
- Demonstrate cost per 1M impressions and a realistic Dedicated capacity plan.
- Provide concrete rollout plan for phase-1 production (canary + autoscale config + fallback model).
- Deliver a short playbook for reranking, caching, and prompt templates used in evaluation.

Scope of work (6-week pilot):
1) Week 0 (prep): access, sample data, env setup
   - Customer provides representative sample impression logs (1M events) and example creatives/metadata.
   - Redwood provisions a dedicated sandbox project (hosted sandbox) and creates API keys + observability hooks.

2) Week 1–2 (integration + model onboarding):
   - Lightweight feature extraction service (edge-friendly): map impression payload to model input (TTL: 3 days).
   - Onboard two model variants: small quantized cross-encoder for reranking (Q4/QLite), and a larger contextual personalization generator for creatives scoring (FP16).
   - Implement prefix KV caching for repeated user-contexts.

3) Week 3 (load bench & latency tuning):
   - Synthetic traffic replay at 3x expected RPS to validate batching and tail latency.
   - Tune batching windowing and autoscaling policies; evaluate response-time vs tokens tradeoff.

4) Week 4 (A/B experiment):
   - Run A/B test comparing current DSP heuristic vs Redwood scoring on sample campaigns (statistical test design included).

5) Week 5 (costing & capacity planning):
   - Produce Dedicated capacity recommendation (instance types, GPU counts, expected QPS).
   - Itemize per-million-impression cost under different caching/batching configs.

6) Week 6 (handoff & playbook):
   - Deliver playbook, runbook, and a 60–90 day rollout checklist.
   - Knowledge transfer workshop (2 hours) with engineering + ops.

Deliverables:
- Integration prototype (running in Redwood sandbox) with test harness to replay impressions.
- Latency and cost report: P50/P90/P99, per-route token counts, and cost per 1M impressions.
- Capacity plan for Dedicated (3 scenarios: baseline, 2x, burst).
- Playbook: prompt templates, cache rules, batching configs, fallback model mapping.
- Handoff materials: runbook, Jupyter notebook with evaluation scripts, and workshop recording/notes.

Roles & responsibilities:
- Redwood SE (Aisha + Priya): architecture, model serving config, capacity planning, runbook.
- Customer eng (DSPCo): provide dataset access, signing keys for sandbox, and deploy the feature-extraction adapter to their staging network.
- SRE (Liam): observability hooks, tracing, and error budgeting for the pilot.

Assumptions (callouts):
- Customer will allow realistic traffic replay to sandbox; if only synthetic traces are available, risk to fidelity increases.
- Models used are open or customer-provided; Redwood will recommend two candidates but final selection may require licensing checks.
- Network egress latency from customer edge to Redwood region is 40–80ms typical; customer is responsible for upstream network optimization.

Risks & mitigations:
- Tail latency spikes under real load -> mitigation: enable model fallback (fast, smaller variant) and implement client-side timeout of 250ms.
- Data privacy/regulatory constraints -> mitigation: strip PII at ingestion, support on-prem/private deployment option in phase 2.
- Inconsistent feature format -> mitigation: deliver a lightweight validation schema and a converter utility during Week 0–1.

Pricing & packaging (pilot commercial proposal):
- Fixed-fee Discovery & Integration (weeks 0–2): $35,000 (includes Redwood SE time, sandbox provisioning, two model onboardings).
- Fixed-fee Benchmarking & Playbook (weeks 3–6): $30,000 (load bench, capacity plan, A/B analysis, final playbook).
- Optional Dedicated sizing & procurement advisory (post-pilot): $12,000 (one-time).
- Optional Private/on-prem packaging (if required by DSPCo): T&M estimate starting at $40k + infra quotes.
- Estimate for Dedicated monthly committed cost (example):
   - Baseline (1M qps-equivalent throughput with batching & caching): 4 x A100-40GB equiv, ~ $28k/mo infra; Redwood platform fee + support: $12k/mo -> total ~$40k/mo.
   - 2x baseline: 8 x A100 -> infra ~$56k/mo; platform fee $20k/mo -> total ~$76k/mo.

Payments & milestones:
- 30% on contract signature -> kick off Week 0.
- 40% after successful integration and Week 2 demo.
- 30% on final handoff (Week 6) and acceptance criteria met.

Acceptance criteria:
- Integration prototype processes sample traffic with no critical errors for 48 hours.
- P90 latency <= 200ms on pilot inputs for the chosen production path (or documented fallback behavior in place).
- Cost report delivered and reviewed in the final workshop.

Workshop plan (2-hour kickoff + 2-hour handoff):
- Kickoff agenda (60–120 min): objectives, sample data review, security checklist, integration plan, target SLOs, roles.
- Handoff agenda: demo, capacity plan walkthrough, ops runbook, Q/A, next steps for Dedicated/Private procurement.

Notes to self / open questions (for internal SE team):
- Confirm whether DSPCo requires ads attribution hashing before sending to Redwood (privacy constraint).
- Check with product on any prebuilt adtech scoring models in model catalog (Priya to check).
- Need SRE sign-off on observability retention (at least 30 days telemetry for pilot).

Next steps (for commercial/AE):
1) Send this proposal to DSPCo with a 2-week validity window.
2) Share sample NDA template if required for dataset transfer.
3) Schedule kickoff meeting and technical deep-dive with DSPCo infra team.

Appendix (quick measurement heuristics):
- Impressions -> tokens: expect ~14 tokens per request for compact contextual prompt; larger creative scoring -> 40–120 tokens.
- Caching: user-context TTL 30min typical; will reduce model calls by estimated 18–35% depending on campaign repetition.
- Batching: 5–15ms batching overhead per window; optimal window depends on traffic burstiness.

Draft sign-off:
- Prepared by: Aisha Kapoor (Redwood SE)
- Reviewed by: Liam O'Connor (SRE), Priya Nair (Applied ML), Diego Martinez (GTM)
